nodes.text: Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ be an infinite set. Must there be a set $E\subset \mathbb{R}$ of positive measure which does not contain any set of the shape $aA+b$ for some $a,b\in\mathbb{R}$ and $a\neq 0$?

#120 : [Er74b] [Er81b,p.29] [Er83d] [Er90] [Er97f] [Va99,2.46] combinatorics The Erdős similarity problem. This is true if $A$ is unbounded or dense in some interval. It therefore suffices to prove this when $A=\{a_1>a_2>\cdots\}$ is a countable strictly monotone sequence which converges to $0$. Steinhaus [St20] has proved this is false whenever $A$ is a finite set. This conjecture is known in many special cases (but, for example, it is open when $A=\{1,1/2,1/4,\ldots\}$, which is Problem 94 on Green's open problems list ). For an overview of progress we recommend a nice survey by Svetic [Sv00] on this problem. A survey of more recent progress was written by Jung, Lai, and Mooroogen [JLM24] .
